messages:
noah: Heads-up — starting bring-up for marlin-6.7B in QA. Found a weird license clause that might block commercial hosting. Can legal/devops eyeball?

anya-legal: Which clause? quick skim: if it's 'research-only' or 'non-commercial' that's a hard stop for Redwood Hosted. Private deployments might be OK depending on wording. Paste the snippet if you have it.

jules: Also: if redistribution includes 'modified binaries' does quantized weights count? We're planning a q4bits build to test perf.

li: Ops note: Dedicated is still hosting on our infra (we operate the GPUs), so commercial restriction applies there too. Private (customer-managed infra) is different.

noah: Pasting license excerpt from LICENSE.md in repo:

```
Use and redistribution of this model and associated weights is limited to non-commercial research purposes only. Modified weights, converted formats, and derivatives fall under the same restriction. Attribution to the original authors is required where practicable.
```

anya-legal: Thanks — that "modified weights, converted formats" sentence is explicit. Quantized versions are derivatives and therefore redistribution of them by us would violate the license unless we obtain a commercial license.

jules: That matches my read. So we can't publish a quantized artifact in our hosted model catalog or allow Dedicated customers to download the quantized weights. Private deployments where the customer runs on-prem should be fine if they accept the same license; but we must be careful about the control plane distributing the artifact.

stella: For evals: can we run internal perf/quality benchmarks on the unmodified weights in QA? We need to know if results/publication is allowed.

anya-legal: Internal benchmarking for evaluation is generally allowed under a research exception if it's internal and not commercial distribution. But the license may also ban public benchmarks; check the full license. Do not publish numbers or host model on Hosted API until we get an explicit commercial grant.

li: ops-bot created ticket INF-4212: "marlin-6.7B license & commercial hosting check" and flagged onboarding as blocked.

noah: @jules did you already email upstream about a commercial license?

jules: I sent an initial inquiry to licensing@marlinlab.org yesterday. Short note asking for commercial terms and whether they permit redistribution of quantized/derived formats. No reply yet. I can escalate.

anya-legal: If they offer a paid commercial license, we'll need standard addendum: (a) right to host and distribute quantized derivatives to Dedicated customers, (b) permissive terms for logs/metrics collection, (c) attribution reach — UI text acceptable. I'll draft a template once they respond.

noah: For now I'll stop the q4bits pipeline and mark builds as draft. Also won't push any artifacts to S3 buckets shared outside legal.

jules: Can we at least run closed-door quant experiments in a sandbox that never leaves our VPC? That feels okay for internal dev, but I want legal sign-off.

anya-legal: Internal sandbox runs are ok for debugging. Anything that creates an artifact intended for distribution (even to a customer) is not allowed.

li: ops-bot: INF-4212 updated with tags [blocked][license][onboarding]. Add me and @anya-legal as watchers.

noah: Thanks everyone. @anya-legal — ping me when you have the addendum draft so we can resume onboarding.

anya-legal: Will do. I'll try to get a short note to upstream asking for a comms/licensing contact and CC legal.

jules: FYI I'll attach our benchmark spec and the exact conversion steps to the ticket so legal can review the "derivative" surface area.

stella: Noted — I'll hold off publishing eval charts.

noah: Closing loop: marlin onboarding paused until INF-4212 cleared.

jules: :thumbsup:
